role: The determinism layer: deterministic replacements for every unseeded RNG source (per-role seeders, Math.random streams, name-seeded split Randoms for vanilla static Randoms, UUIDs) and per-role entity-ID ranges for the CLIENT, SERVER, OTHER and RENDER thread roles, so server state never depends on client work or frame count.
used_by: oracle/decomp/determinize.sh (rewrites vanilla RNG sites to call it)
notes: vanilla_hooks is every oracle/src file that names netherite.oracle.Det (mostly from determinize.sh plus the render/thread-role hooks). clinitWatch names the classes whose static initializer draws from a Det stream while a pool initializes every class. NW_JRAND call sites (and --detail's client-entity call sites) are read frame by frame through JavaLangAccess (JDK 8) instead of a full getStackTrace, and the JRAND lines go through a buffered stderr stream flushed at each JRANDMARK and when the rows close (lane/botspeed: identical lines, G6 110 s to 41 s). uuid()'s --detail call sites (Rows x.cnew) skip sun.reflect frames: the JVM's accessor numbering and inflation made two runs differ (lane/rerecaudit). The client consumer pin (lane/clientrand, PIN_*): on the client thread the torch flicker, a spawned item's EntityItem constructor (handleSpawnObject), the particles' Math.random (net.minecraft.client.particle, not EntityPickupFX), their own Randoms (Entity.<init> under EntityFX.<init>) and EffectRenderer.rand take values from TickRandom streams reseeded each client tick from mix(mix(Oracle.seed, 40 + k), Oracle.tick); the shared streams are still drawn, so rows are unchanged. Found by call site (mathPin, birthPin: one stack walk, a run of 8 or 4 served by one); about 3 us per client draw.
